tasks.instructions: Experiment E1 (tests H27): Merge: one per-B dispatcher from r2/r3/r4-e1/r4-e2 kernels and CUTLASS, winners chosen from interleaved same-container runs. 1. Start from r4-e1-tc-pair2-twoacc (it already carries the unchanged r2 tc_small path for B <= 131, the r3 pair kbs2 path for 131 < B <= 256, tc_pair2 for 256 < B <= 512 and CUTLASS 256x192/256x256 for B > 512). Add r4-e2's pair2 kernel (nb=1 and nb=2 modes, with its fixed per-8-column epilogue remap) into the same kernel.cu under distinct symbol names; keep one launch per call, cudaFuncSetAttribute per kernel at module init, binding.cpp unchanged except the dispatch table. 2. In ONE probe process (rebuild CUTLASS TUs and both hand kernels inside the probe; /tmp is not kept), run harness-mode timing (252 MB zero flush, CUPTI or events) interleaved over 3 rounds for every candidate at every B: 373/384: tc_pair2 (r4-e1), nb1 (r4-e2), CUTLASS 256x192; 449/512: tc_pair2, nb1, CUTLASS 256x256; 691: nb2, CUTLASS 256x192; 773/853: nb2, CUTLASS 256x192 and 256x256; 919: nb2, CUTLASS 256x192. Hand kernels report clock64 span and the globaltimer-derived SM clock; for CUTLASS launch a tiny clock64/globaltimer kernel immediately before and after it to record its clock. Report both wall us and cycles-at-clock for every cell. 3. Selection rule per B: pick the lowest cycles at the same clock; if two candidates are within 3% in cycles, pick the one with the lower rented wall time; prefer CUTLASS on a true tie. Note that hand kernels throttle the card to 1.64-1.75 GHz while CUTLASS runs at 1.96 GHz, so wall time alone understates hand-kernel gains; state which rule decided each B. 4. If the r4-e1 portal result has landed, compute its portal/rented ratio at 192/211/449/512 and use it instead of 1.1-1.15 when predicting; record the ratios in findings. 5. Build the final dispatch table, run run_tests (16/16 x 10 rounds), record max |err| vs fp64 per B over 3 draws for every hand-kernel path, confirm one launch per call via the CUPTI discovery list, and confirm the build time of the whole solution (< 120 s). 6. Design card: paths list every B range with its kernel; findings list the full interleaved table with clocks and the per-B decision. Success: run_tests 16/16, one launch; rented same-container vs r2-e1-tc05-ef-small: 192/211 <= -5%, 449/512 <= -8%, 373/384 <= -5% (nb1) and 773/853 <= -4% in cycles at the same clock; emulator >= 0.625 with the hand-kernel paths at a 1.10-1.15 portal ratio; the kernel is submitted to the portal Refuted if: nb1 does not beat tc_pair2 and CUTLASS at 373/384 by >= 3% in the interleaved run (then 373/384 stay on CUTLASS and depend on E2/E3), or the nb2 773/853 gain is < 3% in cycles (then CUTLASS stays at all L > 512) This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s).

Experiment E2 (tests H25): Bisect the 950-clk per-stage floor against CUTLASS's pipeline structure (warp-specialised ring, CTA-local barriers, rotation without waits). Use r4-e3's probe (2SM pair ring, resident and L2-hot fed modes, clock64 + globaltimer, 3 interleaved rounds, 2 launches per config). Fix the cadence at kbs=1 with N=192 (MMA 384 clk, like CUTLASS 256x192 K32) and N=384 (256+128 two accumulators, MMA 768 clk) and measure clk per stage. 1. Isolate rotation vs waits with resident operands: (a) fixed stage, no barriers; (b) rotating stage address over 4 stages, no barriers; (c) rotating + commit to empty barrier + wait on empty S stages back (the current ring); (d) rotating + commit but the empty wait issued only every 2 or 4 stages. Expect (a) ~551-674 from r3; find which step adds the ~300-400 clk. 2. Warp-specialise as CUTLASS does: warp 0 = TMA producer (waits empty with try_wait.parity, expect_tx, issues TMA for both CTAs' slices), warp 1 = MMA issuer (waits full, tcgen05.fence::after_thread_sync, UMMAs, tcgen05.commit to empty with multicast mask 3); no thread does both. Measure fed L2-hot and resident. 3. Barrier scope variants: 1SM 128xN ring with CTA-local commit/wait (no cluster at all) vs the 2SM ring; 2SM with the commit multicast only to the leader and the peer released by a separate CTA-local arrive; try_wait with .acquire.cta vs .acquire.cluster; the full-barrier wait done by all lanes of the MMA warp vs one lane; UMMA issue with and without a preceding tcgen05.fence::before_thread_sync. 4. Read CUTLASS 4.4 sm100 PipelineTmaUmmaAsync and the sm100 TF32 mainloop (collective/sm100_mma_warpspecialized.hpp, pipeline/sm100_pipeline.hpp) and list every ordering difference against our ring (commit form, fence placement, who waits what, expect_tx accounting for the peer's bytes, elect.sync usage); test each difference that is not already covered. 5. For the best variant, feed it real W from DRAM with the harness flush at Bpad 384 and 464 and report clk per k-block and span. Record the container's fixed-stage floor in every table so results are comparable. Success: A ring variant whose per-stage time at N=192 kbs1 is <= 650 clk and at N=384 kbs1 is <= 850 clk (i.e. within 10% of the 768 MMA ideal) with L2-hot feed, and <= 900 with real W from DRAM at Bpad 384; the source of the 300-400 clk is named with an ablation table Refuted if: Every structural variant, including the full warp-specialised CUTLASS-style ring and the 1SM CTA-local ring, stays >= 900 clk per stage at N=192 and N=384: then the floor is a hardware commit-group rate and only larger stages (H26) can hide it; report the fixed-stage no-wait number as the hardware limit This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s).

Experiment E3 (tests H26): 48-k stages (SW128 32-k + SW64 16-k boxes, 3-stage ring) for the two-accumulator pair at Bpad 384 and the nb2 L tiles. 1. Starting from r4-e1's tc_pair2 kernel (two accumulators, kbs1 ring), change the K stage from 32 to 48: per operand per stage two TMA loads, a 32-k box with 128B swizzle into a 1024-B-aligned region and a 16-k box with 64B swizzle into a separate region (W: 128 rows x 128 B + 128 rows x 64 B = 24 KB; emb: 192 rows at Bpad 384 = 36 KB; 60 KB per stage, 3 stages); K = 3072 = 64 stages; expect_tx covers both boxes of both operands (and the peer's bytes on the leader barrier as today). Build two UMMA smem descriptors per operand per stage: the SW128 one advanced by 32 B per K-step for K-steps 0-3 and an SW64 descriptor (SBO = 8 rows x 64 B = 512 B, swizzle mode 64B) advanced by 32 B for K-steps 4-5; 12 UMMAs per stage (6 K-steps x 2 accumulators), one commit per stage. Two TMA maps per operand (box 32-k SW128 and box 16-k SW64, both TFLOAT32 maps). 2. Validate numerically first at Bpad 384 against fp64 (max |err| <= 1.7e-3 on 3 draws, 0 elements outside atol+rtol) before timing; a wrong SW64 descriptor shows up as large errors, so also test a resident-operand unit test with known data. 3. Measure in one probe, interleaved, 3 rounds, with real W from DRAM and the harness flush: clk per 48-k stage and span at 373/384 for k48 st3 vs the r4-e1 kbs1 st4/st5 ring vs r4-e2 nb1, with the SM clock recorded; also try k48 with 2 stages (to show the 3-stage requirement) and kbs1 st4 as control in the same container. 4. If k48 wins at 384 by >= 10% in cycles, apply the same stage to r4-e2's nb2 kernel at Ntile 352/400/432 (691/773/853: emb 176/200/216 rows per CTA = 33-40.5 KB + 24 KB W; 3 stages fit) and to nb1 at Bpad 464 (67.5 KB x 3), and measure the same way against the r4-e2 nb2 ring and CUTLASS. 5. Ship the result as a candidate with dispatch: k48 at the B's where it wins by >= 5% in cycles, everything else as in r4-e1 (B <= 131 unchanged); run_tests 16/16, one launch, max |err| per B. Success: At 373/384: per-stage time <= 1.15 x 1152 clk (span <= 90k clk vs 107-111k for r4-e1, i.e. >= -15% in cycles at the same clock) and run_tests 16/16; a portal prediction of <= 68 us at 373/384 (vs 83); bonus if nb2 at 691-853 drops >= 10% in cycles Refuted if: The k48 3-stage ring with DRAM W runs >= 1350 clk per stage at Bpad 384 (latency-bound with 3 x 60 KB, i.e. no better than 950 per 32-k), or the SW64 descriptor path makes the UMMAs slower than the SW128 path (resident-operand k48 stage > 1250 clk), or the fixed cost of two TMA boxes per operand raises the feed-only per-stage time above 1100 clk This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%.
